prompt: The graph below shows the percentage of households with internet access at home in three countries between 2000 and 2020.
tip: Line graph: önce **genel eğilimi** (hepsi arttı) ve **en çarpıcı farkı** (Türkiye'nin hızlı yükselişi) overview'da ver. Her yılı tek tek sayma; başlangıç, kesişme ve bitiş noktalarını seç. (Veriler alıştırma amaçlıdır.)

chart.title: Households with internet access at home (%)

model:
The line graph compares the proportion of homes with internet access in Sweden, Brazil and Turkey over a twenty-year period from 2000 to 2020.
Overall, home internet access rose considerably in all three countries. Sweden had by far the highest level throughout, although the gap narrowed sharply as Turkey, in particular, experienced remarkably rapid growth after 2004.
In 2000, almost half of Swedish households (48%) were already connected, compared with only 10% in Brazil and 7% in Turkey. Swedish access then climbed steadily, reaching 84% in 2008 before levelling off in the mid-nineties and ending the period at 96%.
The two other countries followed different paths. Turkey's figure barely changed in the first four years but then rose dramatically, overtaking Brazil in 2012 (47% versus 40%) and almost reaching the Swedish level by 2020, at 90%. Brazil's growth, by contrast, was more gradual but consistent, with the proportion of connected households increasing every year to 71% by the end of the period, which was still the lowest of the three.
modelNotes: Overview ikinci paragrafta ve iki ana bilgiyi veriyor: herkes arttı + Türkiye'nin hızlı yükselişi.
Veriler gruplanmış: Sweden ayrı, Turkey/Brazil karşılaştırmalı.
Farklı trend dili: climbed steadily, levelling off, rose dramatically, overtaking, gradual but consistent.
Kişisel yorum yok; yalnızca veriye dayalı karşılaştırma.
band6:
The graph shows the percentage of households who have internet in Sweden, Brazil and Turkey from 2000 to 2020.
In 2000 Sweden was 48%, Brazil was 10% and Turkey was 7%. In 2004 Sweden increased to 72%, Brazil increased to 16% and Turkey increased to 9%. In 2008 Sweden was 84% and Brazil and Turkey were both 25%.
In 2012 Sweden increased to 92%, Turkey increased to 47% and Brazil increased to 40%. In 2016 Turkey increased a lot and it was 76%, and Brazil was 55%. Sweden was 94%.
In 2020 Sweden was 96%, Turkey was 90% and Brazil was 71%. In conclusion, all the countries increased and Sweden was the highest.
